name: Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type 2

criteria.description: Early-onset distal sensory loss predominantly affecting pain and temperature modalities
Presence of autonomic disturbances including anhidrosis and cardiovascular dysregulation
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the WNK1/HSN2 gene
Lack of significant motor neuropathy or weakness
Nerve biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated fibers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset sensory loss and autonomic dysfunction with genetic confirmation of WNK1/HSN2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by clinical features and confirmed by molecular genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal loss of pain and temperature sensation

pathognomonic.notes: Due to sensory loss leading to unnoticed trauma

laboratory: Reduced or absent sweat response on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing
Nerve conduction studies showing absent or reduced sensory nerve action potentials
imaging: MRI may show normal peripheral nerves; muscle MRI may show mild atrophy in advanced cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in WNK1/HSN2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating loss of small unmyelinated fibers
Nerve biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including renal and cardiac manifestations

redFlags: Early onset of painless injuries with ulcerations
Progressive autonomic dysfunction including orthostatic hypotension
Family history of similar neuropathic symptoms with autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Dyck PJ, et al. Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies: clinical features and molecular genetics. Brain. 2011.
Rotthier A, et al. Genes and mechanisms in hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies. Nat Rev Neurol. 2012.
